skills.title: 02 landline region group
skills.trainingNote: 02 landlines usually indicate NSW or the ACT. Numbering areas cross state borders, so use other clues to choose the state. Ignore 04 mobiles and 13/18 service numbers.
scoringCaveats: These source examples teach recognition; they are not independent unseen assessments.
skills.attributionHtml: Original Fieldwork teaching note. Phone examples from Area Codes (World - ALM) by ValP; schematic reference image hosted by Learnable Meta, linked by the source to Plonk It. Original image rights apply.

skills.title: 03 landline region group
skills.trainingNote: 03 landlines usually indicate Victoria or Tasmania, with border-area exceptions. Separate those states using the scene and infrastructure. The reference map is schematic, not an exact boundary.
scoringCaveats: These source examples teach recognition; they are not independent unseen assessments.
skills.attributionHtml: Original Fieldwork teaching note. Phone examples from Area Codes (World - ALM) by ValP; schematic reference image hosted by Learnable Meta, linked by the source to Plonk It. Original image rights apply.

skills.title: 07 landline region group
skills.trainingNote: 07 landlines support Queensland and nearby numbering-border areas. Read the actual leading digits; 04 is a mobile prefix and does not identify a region.
scoringCaveats: These source examples teach recognition; they are not independent unseen assessments.
skills.attributionHtml: Original Fieldwork teaching note. Phone examples from Area Codes (World - ALM) by ValP; schematic reference image hosted by Learnable Meta, linked by the source to Plonk It. Original image rights apply.

skills.title: 08 landline region group
skills.trainingNote: 08 is shared by WA, SA and the NT, and parts of western NSW. It narrows a broad area, not one state. The reference map simplifies the true numbering boundaries.
scoringCaveats: These source examples teach recognition; they are not independent unseen assessments.
skills.attributionHtml: Original Fieldwork teaching note. Phone examples from Area Codes (World - ALM) by ValP; schematic reference image hosted by Learnable Meta, linked by the source to Plonk It. Original image rights apply.

skills.title: Canberra numbered route shields
skills.trainingNote: These Canberra examples use black numbers in pointed hexagonal shields. Recognize the complete numbered-panel pattern and combine it with city context; a hexagonal shape alone is not ACT-exclusive. Older route markers may remain in historical imagery.
scoringCaveats: These source examples teach recognition; they are not independent unseen assessments.
skills.attributionHtml: Original Fieldwork teaching note. Regional reference: Definitive Australia Guide 2022 by zi8gzag, Eddie, Macca and Denis. Reference images, where shown, are hosted by GeoHints; original rights apply.

skills.title: Queensland high-set housing
skills.trainingNote: Look for an elevated living floor, light timber-style cladding, stairs and a veranda. The space below may be open or enclosed; roof materials vary. This is a Queensland tendency, with similar houses elsewhere, especially northern NSW.
scoringCaveats: These source examples teach recognition; they are not independent unseen assessments.
skills.attributionHtml: Original Fieldwork teaching note. Regional reference: Definitive Australia Guide 2022 by zi8gzag, Eddie, Macca and Denis. Reference images, where shown, are hosted by GeoHints; original rights apply.

skills.title: Darwin-area long-arm streetlights
skills.trainingNote: Look for a long, straight, gently rising arm attached below a short mast-top stub. Single- and twin-arm versions occur. Use this as supporting Darwin-area evidence; neither the arm shape nor a replacement LED head proves a state.
scoringCaveats: These source examples teach recognition; they are not independent unseen assessments.
skills.attributionHtml: Original Fieldwork teaching note. Regional reference: Definitive Australia Guide 2022 by zi8gzag, Eddie, Macca and Denis. Reference images, where shown, are hosted by GeoHints; original rights apply.
